decisions.reason: The source changes hard-return spacing for continuous text; it does not change the separate requirement for predictable legacy-to-new copy-paste behavior.
The line-break spacing decision does not alter the requirement that pasted tables and columns remain within page bounds.
The source explicitly distinguishes excessive spacing in continuous text from spacing between bullet points and does not change the required bullet appearance.

The candidate already requires Enter-based multiline input from the same message; the newly specified hard-return spacing is owned by the paragraph and line-break Requirement and does not change the candidate's state.
Fixed margins and prevention of pencil-icon clipping remain required independently of the paragraph-spacing change.
The permitted theme-color palette is unrelated to hard-return spacing and remains unchanged.
The unintended border created after a Topic row is a separate row-extension behavior, not a consequence of the continuous-text spacing requirement.
Automatic clearing of placeholder text is addressed by separate clauses in the message and is not changed by the paragraph line-break decision.
The source decision does not add, remove, or change any required style-set entry or template-coverage rule.
Customer feedback about paragraph behavior does not alter the earlier task-local due-diligence assessment outputs or method.
The choice of a robust editable-field mechanism is independent of hard-return spacing in continuous text.
The change concerns paragraph returns and spacing, not Tab-controlled list levels or hierarchy alignment.
